title: A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number
main_claim: There is an absolute C such that ℓ(G) ≤ C·h(G) for every finite graph, which is linear list Hadwiger (Kawarabayashi–Mohar). Ordinary linear Hadwiger follows as a corollary.
coverage:
I read all of sections 1–8 line by line. I re-derived the main constant inequalities and checked a few numerics by hand.

Section 3 (the new small-graph argument):
- Bounded sampling: the mass bound ≤ 2 holds.
- Cut-test lemma: the matching existence, the k/3 side sizes, the s-draw domination and the final covering contradiction all hold.
- Uniform concentration: the bounded differences are 2M with M ≤ 2t^{0.1}y, and the exponent is ≥ t^{0.7}.
- Separator-tree localization: the O(n²) node count holds. The blow-up F^(m) argument works: χ ≥ m·f, slot rounding gives the leaf colourings, and the k'-connected J cannot cross a blown-up separator.
- Private sets: the conditional Markov bound 4(q−1)p is correct, and restricting dual weights keeps them feasible. With Reed–Seymour this gives K_{2x} models.
- Complement connectivity via the cut test holds.
- Final K_t assembly: the block/pair assignment uses ≤ q models, and the port and grouping budgets hold.
- Bin partition: 2^u·e^{-Lu/2D} ≤ e^{-u}; the stage sums are O(t); cleanup costs t^{-8} per vertex.

Section 4: the Girão–Narayanan-type constrained colouring induction checks, including the budget inequalities, the promotion step at most 5k−1 < m+6k, and the second-side cost < 2k². So do list extraction, the K_t-subdivision injection bound C(|X|,2), and the additive deletion. Reservation is global, so vertices in T lose ≤ 4Lt colours and vertices outside T lose < t.

Section 5: the coarse density bound checks (constant 7272), as do the incidence lemma (batch sampling, contraction-gain count), Mader's lemma, and the district lemma. In the district lemma I checked the bad-set bound 6nt^{-3ε}, the edge count e(R−B) > dn/2, the peeling charge, the maximality u < p0, the |N∩S| ≥ |N|/16 bound, and the order bound D_K·t^{1.045}.

Section 6: Menger/flow, double packing, rooting (minimal double system, at most two overlapping sets per vertex), rerouting, small-district wovenness (random split, cut test, grouping budget), unpaired path minimization (three-neighbour shortcut and cyclic suffix exchange for degeneracy) and the combine lemma (congestion-2 packing) all check.

Section 7: in the footprint lemma, the stripped first paths and the second paths are each disjoint, exceptional vertices are counted per snapshot via contraction, |X| ≤ t^{1.1}, external degree is ≤ 6B_*t, and the phase-ordered degeneracy is (6B_*+20)t. In separability, the overlap claim |H∩H'| ≥ k comes from the anti-separability supposition. The union is k-connected, the combine/rerouting/grouping steps preserve disjointness, and the invariant H^+ with V(H^+)∩F^+ = W^+ is restored. The S inequalities are consistent.

Section 8: the proxies, the large-minor rooted case, the base range via coarse density, the junction district, the d=42 deletion, combining, the 3-district recursion with a' = 2⌈a/3⌉ and its arithmetic Q(a−a')−Aa−6Ka' > 0, the weaving capacity 2a ≤ 3a', the disjointness of designated bags from foreign paths, and the final t = h+1 step all check.

Not independently verified (taken as cited): Reed–Seymour f ≤ 2h; the Girão–Narayanan ordinary extraction in the stated 7k/6k form; and the Bollobás–Thomason/Delcourt–Postle grouping theorem with a uniform γ.
sibling_notes: The only family-157 sibling on the board was the Colin de Verdière counterexample (no_gap_found). This paper cites the companion Hadwiger-counterexample paper only for motivation in the introduction, so the proof has no circular dependence on it. I posted a summary to the board.
